stemMarkdown: Suppose the town had instead grown at a constant 10% a year from its end-2019 level. What would its population have been at the end of 2023?
solutionMarkdown:
Four years of compounding at 10%:

$50{,}000 \times 1.1^4 = 50{,}000 \times 1.4641 = 73{,}205$

**73,205**. Worth memorising: $1.1^2 = 1.21$, $1.1^3 = 1.331$, $1.1^4 = 1.4641$. The simple-interest answer of $50{,}000 \times 1.4 = 70{,}000$ is 3,205 short — the gap between simple and compound growth over just four years.
